label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let $0<s<1$, and let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be $s$-Frostman probability measures on $[0,1]$.
If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:profile-separation}
  \limsup_{t\to\infty}\abs{H_{\mu_1}^s(t)-H_{\mu_2}^s(t)}>0,
\end{equation}
then
\[
  \operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_1)\perp\operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_2)
  \quad\text{on }\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^2).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:profile-asymptotics
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:profile-asymptotics}
Let $\mu$ be the natural self-similar probability measure of an IFS satisfying the open set
condition, with similarity dimension $s\in(0,1)$.
If the IFS is of lattice type with span $\ell$, then there is a continuous, strictly positive,
non-constant $\ell/2$-periodic function $\widetilde H_\mu^s$ such that
\[
  H_\mu^s(t)-\widetilde H_\mu^s(t)\to0
  \qquad\text{as }t\to\infty.
\]
If the IFS is of non-lattice type, then
\[
  H_\mu^s(t)\to C_\mu\in(0,\infty)
  \qquad\text{as }t\to\infty.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:cantor-application
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{thm:cantor-application}
Let $\mu_A$ and $\mu_B$ be the natural self-similar probability measures of two IFSs on $[0,1]$
satisfying the open set condition, with common similarity dimension $s\in(0,1)$. If the first
IFS is of lattice type and the second is of non-lattice type, then
\[
  \operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_A)\perp\operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_B).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:fixed-dimension-separation
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fixed-dimension-separation}
Let $s\in(0,1)$. For every $p_1\in(0,1/2]$, the set of $p_2\in(0,1/2]$ with
$\overline H_s(p_2)=\overline H_s(p_1)$ is finite. Consequently, for $p_2\in(0,1/2]$ not in this
exceptional set,
$\overline H_s(p_1)\neq\overline H_s(p_2)$, and
\[
  \operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_{p_1})\perp\operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_{p_2}).
\]
The set $D_s$ has no accumulation point in $(0,1/2]$, and the mean is strictly monotone on
every component of $(0,1/2)\setminus D_s$.
head: environment

label: thm:small-dimension-monotone
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:small-dimension-monotone}
There exists $s_0\in(0,1)$ such that, for every $s\in(0,s_0]$, the mean
$p\mapsto\overline H_s(p)$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1/2]$. Consequently, for all distinct
$p_1,p_2\in(0,1/2]$,
\[
  \operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_{p_1})\perp\operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_{p_2}).
\]

title: Corollary

For every $s\in(0,1)$ and all $p_1,p_2\in(0,1/2]$ with
$\overline H_s(p_1)\neq\overline H_s(p_2)$,

  \operatorname{Law}(W(K_{p_1}))\perp\operatorname{Law}(W(K_{p_2}))

label: thm:gaussian-reduction
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $u\neq t$, the increment $W_u-W_t$ is a centred planar Gaussian with covariance
$\abs{u-t}I_2$. Polar integration gives
\[
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{W_u-W_t}<r)=1-\exp\left(-\frac{r^2}{2\abs{u-t}}\right).
\]
Since $\mu$ is atomless, this holds for $\mu\times\mu$-almost every $(u,t)$.
Integrating with respect to $\mu\times\mu$ and applying Fubini's theorem gives the first
identity, while pushing $\mu\times\mu$ forward by $(u,t)\mapsto\abs{u-t}$ gives the second.
head: environment

label: thm:renewal-defect-left-tail
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:renewal-defect-left-tail}
The function $z(t)$ is continuous and for $t\leqslant0$,
\[
  z(t)=e^{st}\left(1-\sum_i r_i^{2s}\right)>0.
\]
In particular, $z(t)$ decays exponentially as $t\to-\infty$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Continuity follows from $z(t)=G(t)-\sum_i p_iG(t-\alpha_i)$, since $G$ is continuous,
and non-negativity follows from the definition of the cross term. For $t\leqslant0$, every
pair lies within distance $e^{-t}\geqslant1$, so
\[
  \mathcal{C}^\times_{e^{-t}}(\mu)=\sum_{i\neq j}p_ip_j=1-\sum_i p_i^2.
\]
The claim follows because $p_i=r_i^s\in(0,1)$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$.
head: environment

label: thm:cross-piece-mass
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:boundary-mass
title: Proof
body_md:
By Ahlfors regularity, for each $x\in K$ the $\mu$-mass of points $y$ satisfying
  $\abs{S_i(x)-S_j(y)}\leqslant\delta$ is at most $C\delta^s$, and it vanishes unless
  $\operatorname{dist}(S_i(x),S_jK)\leqslant\delta$. Fubini's theorem gives
  \[
    \mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu)\leqslant C\delta^s\sum_{i\neq j}p_ip_j\,
    \mu\set{x\in K\colon\operatorname{dist}(S_i(x),S_jK)\leqslant\delta},
  \]
  so it suffices to prove, for some $\eta\in(0,1-s)$,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-mass}
    \mu\set{x\in K\colon\operatorname{dist}(S_i(x),S_jK)\leqslant\delta}
    \leqslant C\delta^\eta,\qquad0<\delta\leqslant1,\quad i\neq j.
  \end{equation}
  By Schief~\cite{Schief1994} the IFS satisfies the strong open set condition, so
  Lalley's estimate~\cite[Proposition~3]{Lalley1988} applies: there is $\gamma>0$
  such that every $\delta$-separated subset of
  $A_{ij}(\delta)=\set{y\in S_iK\colon\operatorname{dist}(y,S_jK)\leqslant\delta}$ has at most
  $C\delta^{\gamma-s}$ points. The closed balls of radius $\delta$ about a maximal
  $\delta$-separated subset cover $A_{ij}(\delta)$, and each has $\mu$-mass at most
  $C\delta^s$ by Ahlfors regularity, so $\mu(A_{ij}(\delta))\leqslant C\delta^\gamma$.
  Since $\mu(S_iA)\geqslant p_i\mu(A)$ for every Borel set $A$ by self-similarity,
  \cref{eq:boundary-mass} follows with $\eta=\min\set{\gamma,(1-s)/2}$, and with it
  \cref{eq:cross-piece-mass}.
  Taking $\delta=e^{-t}$ and multiplying by $e^{st}$ gives the bound on $z$.
head: environment

label: thm:renewal-limits
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:renewal-limits}
  If the IFS is of non-lattice type, then
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:g-non-lattice-limit}
    G(t)\to\frac{1}{m}\int_{\mathbb{R}}z(x)\,\mathrm{d} x\in(0,\infty),
    \qquad t\to\infty.
  \end{equation}
  If the IFS is of lattice type with span $\ell$, then $\widetilde G$ is continuous,
  strictly positive and $\ell$-periodic, and
  \[
    G(t)-\widetilde G(t)\to0,\qquad t\to\infty.
  \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{thm:renewal-defect-left-tail,thm:cross-piece-mass}, the defect $z$ satisfies the
hypotheses above. Since $G$ is bounded and tends to zero at $-\infty$, the renewal theorem
gives \cref{eq:g-non-lattice-limit} and the lattice approximation. Positivity of the integral
and of $\widetilde G$ follows from $z\geqslant0$ and $z(t)>0$ for $t\leqslant0$.
head: environment

label: thm:lattice-nonconvergence
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:lattice-nonconvergence}
If the IFS is of lattice type, then the periodic profile $\widetilde G$ is non-constant.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $i\neq j$. The maps $S_{ij}$ and $S_{ji}$ have the contraction ratio, while their
images must be non-trivially translationally separated by the open set condition.
So, there exists $\rho\coloneqq\abs{S_{ij}(0)-S_{ji}(0)}>0$.

For $0<\delta<\rho/(2r_{ij})$, put $\delta_1=\rho-2r_{ij}\delta$ and
$\delta_2=\rho+r_{ij}\delta$. We have
$\delta_1<\abs{S_{ij}(x)-S_{ji}(y)}\leqslant\delta_2$.
Expanding the difference $\mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_2}(\mu)-\mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_1}(\mu)$ therefore gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_2}(\mu)-\mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_1}(\mu)
  &\geqslant p_i^2p_j^2(\mu\times\mu)
    \set{(x,y)\colon\delta_1<\abs{S_{ij}(x)-S_{ji}(y)}\leqslant\delta_2}\\*
  &\geqslant p_i^2p_j^2\mathcal{C}_\delta(\mu).
\end{align*}
Hence,
\begin{align*}
  \delta_2^s\widetilde G(-\log\delta_2)-\delta_1^s\widetilde G(-\log\delta_1)
  &=\frac{\ell}{m}\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}e^{sk\ell}
    \bigl(\mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_2e^{-k\ell}}(\mu)-\mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta_1e^{-k\ell}}(\mu)\bigr)\\*
  &\geqslant\frac{\ell}{m} p_i^2p_j^2\mathcal{C}_\delta(\mu)\geqslant c\delta^s.
\end{align*}
Since $\widetilde G$ is bounded and $\delta_2^s-\delta_1^s=O(\delta)$, this gives
\[
  \delta_2^s\bigl(\widetilde G(-\log\delta_2)-\widetilde G(-\log\delta_1)\bigr)
  \geqslant c\delta^s-C\delta>0
\]
for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, since $s<1$.

label: thm:smoothing-injective
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:fourier-multiplier
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $g$ is $\ell$-periodic, its Fourier coefficients are
\[
  \widehat g(k)=\frac1\ell\int_0^\ell g(x)e^{-2\pi ikx/\ell}\,\mathrm{d} x,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}.
\]
The $\ell$-periodic function $x\mapsto Tg(x/2)=\int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)g(x-\log\eta)\,\mathrm{d}\eta$
is an average of translates of $g$. Translating $g$ by $\log\eta\in\mathbb{R}$ multiplies
$\widehat g(k)$ by $e^{-2\pi ik\log(\eta)/\ell}=\eta^{-2\pi ik/\ell}$. 
Averaging over $\eta$, Fubini's theorem gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fourier-multiplier}
  \widehat{Tg}(k)=\left(\int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)\eta^{-2\pi ik/\ell}\,\mathrm{d}\eta\right)\widehat g(k),
  \qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},
\end{equation}
where $\widehat{Tg}(k)$ denotes the $k$-th Fourier coefficient of $Tg$ with respect to
its period $\ell/2$.

The multiplier, when substituting $x=1/(2\eta)$, becomes
\[
  \int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)\eta^{-2\pi ik/\ell}\,\mathrm{d}\eta
  =2^{-s+2\pi ik/\ell}\int_0^\infty x^{-s+2\pi ik/\ell}e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d} x.
\]
The last integral is $\Gamma(z)=\int_0^\infty x^{z-1}e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d} x$ for
$z=1-s+2\pi ik/\ell$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma-multiplier}
  \int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)\eta^{-2\pi ik/\ell}\,\mathrm{d}\eta
  =2^{-s+2\pi ik/\ell}\Gamma(1-s+2\pi ik/\ell),
\end{equation}
which is non-zero.

Now let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be continuous and $\ell$-periodic with $Tg_1=Tg_2$. Linearity
gives $T(g_1-g_2)=0$, so by \cref{eq:fourier-multiplier} and the non-vanishing of the
multipliers, $\widehat{(g_1-g_2)}(k)=0$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. By the uniqueness theorem
$g_1=g_2$, so $T$ is injective. The conclusion on constant functions follows directly from the
non-vanishing of multipliers.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In the non-lattice case, \cref{thm:renewal-limits} and dominated convergence in
\cref{eq:h-definition} give
\[
  H_\mu^s(t)\to\frac1m\int_\mathbb{R} z(x)\,\mathrm{d} x
    \int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)\,\mathrm{d}\eta\in(0,\infty).
\]

In the lattice case with span $\ell$, let $\widetilde G$ be the periodic limit from
\cref{thm:renewal-limits} and put $\widetilde H_\mu^s=T\widetilde G$. This function is
continuous, strictly positive, and $\ell/2$-periodic, and it is non-constant by
\cref{thm:lattice-nonconvergence,thm:smoothing-injective}. Since $G$ and $\widetilde G$ are
bounded, dominated convergence gives
\[
  H_\mu^s(t)-\widetilde H_\mu^s(t)
  =\int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)
    \bigl(G(2t-\log\eta)-\widetilde G(2t-\log\eta)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\eta
  \to0.\qedhere
\]

label: thm:four-point-integral
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:four-point-integral}
There is a constant $C>0$, depending only on $s$ and $A$, such that, for every $0<r\leqslant1$,
\[
  \int_{\set{I\cap I'\neq\varnothing}}
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^4
  \leqslant C V_s(r).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mu$ is non-atomic, we may ignore tuples with repeated endpoints. For overlapping
intervals, put
\[
  a=|I\cap I'|\quad\text{and}\quad b=|I\mathbin{\triangle}I'|.
\]
The coordinate pairs $(Z_1,Z'_1)$ and $(Z_2,Z'_2)$ are independent centred Gaussian vectors,
each with covariance matrix
\[
  \begin{pmatrix}|I|&\pm a\\\pm a&|I'|\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The determinant of this matrix is
\[
  |I||I'|-a^2=ab+(|I|-a)(|I'|-a)\geqslant ab>0.
\]
Hence the joint density $f$ of $(Z,Z')$ satisfies
\[
  f(z,z')\leqslant\frac{1}{(2\pi)^2(|I||I'|-a^2)}\leqslant\frac{1}{(2\pi)^2ab}.
\]
Hence
\[
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)
  =\int_{B(0,r)}\int_{B(0,r)}f(z,z')\,\mathrm{d} z'\,\mathrm{d} z
  \leqslant\frac{(\pi r^2)^2}{(2\pi)^2ab}
  =\frac{r^4}{4ab}.
\]
We may assume, relabelling if necessary, that $|I|\geqslant|I'|$, so $|I|\geqslant(a+b)/2$. Since
\[
  \{\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r\}\subseteq\{\abs{Z}<r\},
\]
we obtain
\[
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)
  \leqslant\int_{B(0,r)}\frac{e^{-\abs{z}^2/(2|I|)}}{2\pi|I|}\,\mathrm{d} z
  =1-e^{-r^2/(2|I|)}
  \leqslant\frac{r^2}{2|I|}\leqslant\frac{r^2}{a+b}.
\]
Together with the trivial full probability bound, these inequalities yield
\begin{align*}
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)
  &\leqslant\min\left\{1,\frac{r^2}{a+b},\frac{r^4}{4ab}\right\}\\
  &\leqslant\min\left\{1,\frac{r^2}{a},\frac{r^2}{b},\frac{r^4}{ab}\right\}
  =\min\left\{1,\frac{r^2}{a}\right\}\min\left\{1,\frac{r^2}{b}\right\}.
\end{align*}

The Frostman bound and $\mu(\mathbb{R})=1$ give, for $a,b>0$,
\[
  \mu^4\set{0<|I\cap I'|<a,\ |I\mathbin{\triangle}I'|<b}
  \leqslant4!A^3\min\{1,a\}^s\min\{1,b\}^{2s}.
\]
These bounds and Fubini's theorem give
\begin{align*}
  \int_{\set{I\cap I'\neq\varnothing}}
    \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^4
  &\leqslant r^4\int_{r^2}^\infty\int_{r^2}^\infty
    \mu^4\set{0<|I\cap I'|<a,\ |I\mathbin{\triangle}I'|<b}
    \frac{\,\mathrm{d} b\,\mathrm{d} a}{a^2b^2}\\
  &\leqslant4!A^3
    \left(r^2\int_{r^2}^\infty\frac{\min\{1,a\}^s}{a^2}\,\mathrm{d} a\right)
    \left(r^2\int_{r^2}^\infty\frac{\min\{1,b\}^{2s}}{b^2}\,\mathrm{d} b\right).
\end{align*}
Their product is at most $C V_s(r)$, since
\begin{align*}
  r^2\int_{r^2}^\infty\frac{\min\{1,a\}^s}{a^2}\,\mathrm{d} a
  &=r^2+r^2\int_{r^2}^1a^{s-2}\,\mathrm{d} a
  =\frac{r^{2s}-sr^2}{1-s}\leqslant\frac{r^{2s}}{1-s},
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
  r^2\int_{r^2}^\infty\frac{\min\{1,b\}^{2s}}{b^2}\,\mathrm{d} b
  &=r^2+r^2\int_{r^2}^1b^{2s-2}\,\mathrm{d} b\\*
  &\leqslant
  \begin{cases}
    r^{4s}/(1-2s),&0<s<1/2,\\
    r^2(1+2\log(1/r)),&s=1/2,\\
    2sr^2/(2s-1),&1/2<s<1.
  \end{cases}
\end{align*}
These are the required bounds, up to a multiplicative factor.

label: thm:variance
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:variance}
Let $0<s<1$ and let $\mu$ be an $s$-Frostman probability measure on $[0,1]$ with Frostman
constant $A\geqslant1$. There is a constant $C>0$, depending only on $s$ and $A$, such that
\[
  \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\mathcal{C}_r(W_*\mu)\bigr)\leqslant C V_s(r),
  \qquad 0<r\leqslant1.
\]
Moreover, $V_s(r)=o(r^{4s})$ as $r\to0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Expanding the variance and applying Fubini's theorem gives
\[
  \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\mathcal{C}_r(W_*\mu)\bigr)=\int\left(
  \mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)
  -\mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r)\mathbb{P}(\abs{Z'}<r)
  \right)\,\mathrm{d}\mu^4.
\]
By independence of disjoint Brownian increments, the integrand vanishes when
$I\cap I'=\varnothing$. Otherwise it is at most $\mathbb{P}(\abs{Z}<r,\abs{Z'}<r)$, so
\cref{thm:four-point-integral} gives the variance bound. In each case of
\cref{eq:variance-scale}, $V_s(r)/r^{4s}\to0$ as $r\to0$.
head: environment

label: thm:uniform-concentration
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:uniform-concentration}
Let $0<s<1$ and let $\mu$ be an $s$-Frostman probability measure on $[0,1]$. Then
\[
  \limsup_{t\to\infty}\abs{Y_\mu(t)-H_\mu^s(t)}=0
  \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
head: environment

label: eq:grid-convergence
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an integer $m\geqslant1$ and put $t_{j,m}\coloneqq j/m$. By \cref{eq:y-variance},
\[
  \sum_{j=0}^\infty\operatorname{Var}(Y_\mu(t_{j,m}))<\infty.
\]
One can then estimate $\mathbb{P}\{\abs{Y_\mu(t)-H_\mu^s(t)}>\varepsilon\}$ by Chebyshev's inequality and apply
the Borel--Cantelli lemma, giving
\begin{equation}\label{eq:grid-convergence}
  Y_\mu(t_{j,m})-H_\mu^s(t_{j,m})\to0
  \qquad\text{almost surely as }j\to\infty.
\end{equation}

If $t\in[t_{j,m},t_{j+1,m}]$, monotonicity of $r\mapsto\mathcal{C}_r(W_*\mu)$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:monotone-fill}
  e^{-2s/m}Y_\mu(t_{j+1,m})\leqslant Y_\mu(t)\leqslant e^{2s/m}Y_\mu(t_{j,m}).
\end{equation}
Combining \cref{eq:grid-convergence,eq:monotone-fill} gives, almost surely,
\[
  \limsup_{t\to\infty}\abs{Y_\mu(t)-H_\mu^s(t)}
  \leqslant (e^{2s/m}-1)\sup_{t\geqslant0}H_\mu^s(t)
  +\sup_{\substack{t,u\geqslant0\\\abs{t-u}\leqslant1/m}}
  \abs{H_\mu^s(t)-H_\mu^s(u)}.
\]
Taking the countable intersection over $m$ and using the boundedness of $H_\mu^s$
and its uniform continuity from \cref{eq:h-definition} gives the desired limit.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $i\in\set{1,2}$, define
\[
  \mathcal{E}_i\coloneqq
  \set{\nu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^2)\colon
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\substack{q\in\mathbb{Q}\\q\geqslant n}}
  \abs{e^{2sq}\mathcal{C}_{e^{-q}}(\nu)-H_{\mu_i}^s(q)}=0}.
\]
Each $\mathcal{E}_i$ is Borel, since $\nu\mapsto\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)$ is Borel for every $r>0$.
Suppose that $\nu\in\mathcal{E}_1\cap\mathcal{E}_2$. The triangle inequality gives
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\substack{q\in\mathbb{Q}\\q\geqslant n}}
  \abs{H_{\mu_1}^s(q)-H_{\mu_2}^s(q)}=0.
\]
Both expected profiles are uniformly continuous by \cref{eq:h-definition}.
Density of the rationals therefore implies $H_{\mu_1}^s(t)-H_{\mu_2}^s(t)\to0$ as
$t\to\infty$, contradicting the assumption of distinct profiles, \cref{eq:profile-separation}. Hence
$\mathcal{E}_1\cap\mathcal{E}_2=\varnothing$. 

Further, by \cref{thm:uniform-concentration},
\[
  \operatorname{Law}(W_*\mu_i)(\mathcal{E}_i)=1.
\]
Hence the two laws give
full measure to the respective disjoint Borel sets $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$, which proves
that they are mutually singular.

title: Proof
body_md:
The IFS defining $\mu_A$ is of lattice type, so \cref{thm:profile-asymptotics}
gives a non-constant periodic asymptotic profile for $H_{\mu_A}^s$, while $H_{\mu_B}^s$ converges

label: thm:neighbourhood-moments
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:neighbourhood-stopping-count
title: Proof
body_md:
We apply the stopping construction of \cref{eq:stopping-family} at scale $r^2$, giving
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neighbourhood-stopping-count}
  \#\mathcal{W}(r^2)\leqslant Cr^{-2s}.
\end{equation}
For each $w\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)$, choose an endpoint $t_w$ of $S_w([0,1])$ and put
$\omega_w\coloneqq\sup_{t\in S_w([0,1])}\abs{W_t-W_{t_w}}$. The resulting discs
$\overline B(W_{t_w},\omega_w)$ cover $E$. Enlarging their radii by $r$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neighbourhood-cover-bound}
  M_r(E)\leqslant\mathcal{L}^2(\langle E\rangle_r)
  \leqslant\pi\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)}(r+\omega_w)^2.
\end{equation}
Brownian scaling and the maximal inequality give, for every $w\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)$,
\[
  \mathbb{E}(r+\omega_w)^{2q}\leqslant C_qr^{2q}.
\]
By convexity,
\[
  \left(\sum_w(r+\omega_w)^2\right)^q
  \leqslant\bigl(\#\mathcal{W}(r^2)\bigr)^{q-1}\sum_w(r+\omega_w)^{2q}.
\]
Taking expectations and using \cref{eq:neighbourhood-stopping-count,eq:neighbourhood-cover-bound}
proves
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-moment-bound}.

For the lower bound, let $\nu\coloneqqW_*\mu$ and define
$h_{r/2}\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to[0,1]$ by $h_{r/2}(x)\coloneqq\nu(B(x,r/2))$. Since $h_{r/2}$ vanishes
outside $\langle E\rangle_{r/2}$, Fubini's theorem gives
\begin{align*}
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}h_{r/2}(x)\,\mathrm{d} x&=\frac{\pi r^2}{4},\\
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}h_{r/2}(x)^2\,\mathrm{d} x
  &=\iint\mathcal{L}^2(B(y,r/2)\cap B(z,r/2))\,\mathrm{d}\nu(y)\,\mathrm{d}\nu(z)\\
  &\leqslant\frac{\pi r^2}{4}\mathcal{C}_r(\nu).
\end{align*}
Some ball of radius $r/2$ in a finite cover of the support of $\nu$ has positive $\nu$-measure.
Since $\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)\geqslant\nu(B(x,r/2))^2$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^2$, we have $\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)>0$.
Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neighbourhood-correlation-lower-bound}
  \mathcal{L}^2(\langle E\rangle_{r/2})\geqslant\frac{\pi r^2}{4\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)}.
\end{equation}
Since $M_r(E)\geqslant\frac12\mathcal{L}^2(\langle E\rangle_{r/2})$, Jensen's inequality and
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-correlation-lower-bound} give
\[
  \mathbb{E} M_r(E)
  \geqslant\frac{\pi r^2}{8}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)}\right]
  \geqslant\frac{\pi r^2}{8\mathbb{E} \mathcal{C}_r(\nu)}.
\]
For $0<r\leqslant1$, \cref{eq:expected-profile} and the boundedness of $H_\mu^s$ give
$\mathbb{E}\mathcal{C}_r(\nu)\leqslant Cr^{2s}$ and hence \cref{eq:neighbourhood-mean-lower-bound}.

label: thm:neighbourhood-overlap
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:stopping-brownian-overlap
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $i\neq j$. The intersection is contained in $\langle E\rangle_r$, so for $r^2\geqslant r_{\min}$,
\cref{thm:neighbourhood-moments} bounds its expected area by
$Cr^{2-2s}\leqslant Cr_{\min}^{-\eta}r^{2-2s+2\eta}$.
We may therefore assume $r^2<r_{\min}$ and consider the stopping set $\mathcal{W}(r^2)$.
For $w,v\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)$, put
\[
  A_w=\langleW(S_wK)\rangle_r,
  \qquad d_{wv}=\operatorname{dist}(I_w,I_v),
\]
where $I_v = S_v([0,1])$.
Since each interval $I_w$ has length at most $r^2$, the Brownian maximal estimate used in
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-cover-bound} gives $\mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(A_w)\leqslant Cr^2$.
We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stopping-brownian-overlap}
  \mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(A_w\cap A_v)\leqslant\frac{Cr^4}{r^2+d_{wv}}.
\end{equation}
For $d_{wv}\leqslant r^2$, this follows by bounding the intersection by $A_w$.
For $d_{wv}>r^2$, we use the Gaussian-density argument from the proof of
\cref{thm:four-point-integral} which similarly gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(A_w\cap A_v)
  &\leqslant\frac{1}{2\pi d_{wv}}\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{L}^2(A_w)\mathcal{L}^2(A_v)\bigr]\\
  &=\frac{1}{2\pi d_{wv}}
       \mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(A_w)\,\mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(A_v)
  \leqslant\frac{Cr^4}{d_{wv}},
\end{align*}
which proves \cref{eq:stopping-brownian-overlap}.

For $h\geqslant r^2$, let $N_{ij}(h)$ count pairs $(w,v)\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)^2$ whose first
symbols are $i,j$, respectively, and for which $d_{wv}\leqslant h$. Every pair of points in
$S_wK\times S_vK$ then has distance at most $h+2r^2\leqslant3h$.
The cross correlation bound \cref{eq:cross-piece-mass} extends to all positive scales after increasing $C$,
since $\mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu)\leqslant1$.
Decompose with the stopping family
and using $p_wp_v\geqslant r_{\min}^{2s}r^{4s}$, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stopping-close-pairs}
  \begin{split}
    r_{\min}^{2s}r^{4s}N_{ij}(h)
    &\leqslant\sum_{\substack{w,v\in\mathcal{W}(r^2)\\w_1=i,\ v_1=j,\ d_{wv}\leqslant h}}p_wp_v\\
    &\leqslant\mathcal{C}^\times_{3h}(\mu)\leqslant Ch^{s+\eta}.
  \end{split}
\end{equation}

We group the pairs with $d_{wv}\leqslant r^2$ together and use the ranges
$2^{k-1}r^2<d_{wv}\leqslant2^kr^2$ for $k\geqslant1$. Using subadditivity,
\cref{eq:stopping-brownian-overlap,eq:stopping-close-pairs}, and $s+\eta<1$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
  \mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(\langleW(S_iK)\rangle_r\cap\langleW(S_jK)\rangle_r)
  &\leqslant Cr^4\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{N_{ij}(2^kr^2)}{2^kr^2}\\
  &\leqslant Cr^{2-2s+2\eta}\sum_{k=0}^\infty2^{k(s+\eta-1)}
  =\frac{Cr^{2-2s+2\eta}}{1-2^{s+\eta-1}}.
\end{align*}
Lastly, by \cref{eq:neighbourhood-defect-elementary},
\begin{align*}
  \mathbb{E} D_r
  &\leqslant\sum_{1\leqslant i<j\leqslant N}
    \mathbb{E}\mathcal{L}^2(\langleW(S_iK)\rangle_r\cap\langleW(S_jK)\rangle_r)\\
  &\leqslant\frac{C\binom{N}{2}}{1-2^{s+\eta-1}}r^{2-2s+2\eta},
\end{align*}
which finishes the proof.

label: thm:neighbourhood-renewal
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:neighbourhood-renewal-equation
title: Proof
body_md:
The bounds $c\leqslant Q(t)\leqslant C$ follow from \cref{thm:neighbourhood-moments}. Brownian scaling and
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-union-scaling} give, for every $r>0$,
\[
  \mathbb{E} M_r(W(S_i(K)))=r_i\mathbb{E} M_{r/\sqrt{r_i}}(E).
\]
Recall that $\alpha_i=\log(1/r_i)$ and put $d(t)=e^{(2-2s)t}\mathbb{E} D_{e^{-t}}$ for $t\geqslant0$.
The definition of $D_r$ gives, for $t\geqslant\frac12\max_i \alpha_i$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neighbourhood-renewal-equation}
  \begin{split}
    Q(t)
    &=e^{(2-2s)t}\sum_i\mathbb{E} M_{e^{-t}}(W(S_i(K)))-d(t)\\
    &=\sum_i r_i e^{(1-s)\alpha_i}Q(t-\alpha_i/2)-d(t)\\
    &=\sum_i p_i Q(t-\alpha_i/2)-d(t).
  \end{split}
\end{equation}
Moreover, \cref{thm:neighbourhood-overlap} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neighbourhood-renewal-defect}
  0\leqslant d(t)\leqslant Ce^{(2-2s)t}e^{-(2-2s+2\eta)t}=Ce^{-2\eta t},
  \qquad t\geqslant0.
\end{equation}

Continuity of $M_r(E)$ in $r$ and the moment bound in \cref{thm:neighbourhood-moments}
give continuity of $Q$ by dominated convergence. We apply the renewal theorem in the form
\cref{eq:renewal-shift} to $Q$ with interarrival distribution $\sum_i p_i\delta_{\alpha_i/2}$,
using \cref{eq:neighbourhood-renewal-equation,eq:neighbourhood-renewal-defect}, to obtain
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-renewal-shift}.

label: thm:neighbourhood-concentration
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:stopping-neighbourhood-variance
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\gamma<\min\{s,2\eta/3\}$ and put $r=e^{-t}$. For $r_{\min}\leqslant r\leqslant1$,
\cref{thm:neighbourhood-moments} gives
\[
  \operatorname{Var}\bigl(r^{2s-2}M_r(E)\bigr)\leqslant r^{4s-4}\mathbb{E}[M_r(E)^2]\leqslant C
  \leqslant Cr_{\min}^{-\gamma}e^{-\gamma t}.
\]
We may therefore, without loss of generality, assume $0<r<r_{\min}$.
For $w\in\mathcal{W}(r)$, we have $r_w>r_{\min}r>r^2$, so $r/\sqrt{r_w}<1$.
By \cref{eq:cylinder-neighbourhood-scaling,thm:neighbourhood-moments}, for every $q\geqslant1$,
\[
  \mathbb{E}[M_r(W(S_wK))^q]
  \leqslant C_qr_w^q\left(\frac{r}{\sqrt{r_w}}\right)^{q(2-2s)}
  =C_qr^{q(2-2s)}p_w^q.
\]
As in \cref{sec:osc-geometry}, we partition $\mathcal{W}(r)$ into classes
$\mathcal{W}_1(r),\ldots,\mathcal{W}_M(r)$ such that the time intervals $I_w$ have pairwise disjoint interiors
within each class.
By independence within each class, Cauchy--Schwarz, and $p_w\leqslant r^s$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stopping-neighbourhood-variance}
  \begin{split}
    r^{4s-4}\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}M_r(W(S_wK))\right)
    &\leqslant Mr^{4s-4}\sum_{j=1}^M
      \operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}_j(r)}M_r(W(S_wK))\right)\\
    &=Mr^{4s-4}\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}\operatorname{Var}(M_r(W(S_wK)))\\
    &\leqslant C\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}p_w^2
     \leqslant Cr^s\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}p_w=Cr^s.
  \end{split}
\end{equation}

We next bound the total overlap defect. Let $\mathcal{T}(r)$ be the set of proper prefixes of words
in $\mathcal{W}(r)$, including the empty word. For $v\in\mathcal{T}(r)$, put
\[
  D_{v,r}=\sum_i M_r(W(S_vS_iK))-M_r(W(S_vK))\geqslant0.
\]
The terms for internal cylinders cancel, giving
\[
  \sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}D_{v,r}
  =\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}M_r(W(S_wK))-M_r(E).
\]
For $v\in\mathcal{T}(r)$, we have $r_v>r$. Brownian scaling and
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-defect-mean} give
\begin{align*}
  r^{2s-2}\mathbb{E} D_{v,r}
  &=r^{2s-2}r_v\mathbb{E} D_{r/\sqrt{r_v}}
  \leqslant Cr^{2s-2}r_v\left(\frac{r}{\sqrt{r_v}}\right)^{2-2s+2\eta}
   =Cr^{2\eta}p_vr_v^{-\eta}.
\end{align*}
Since $r<r_v\leqslant(\max_i r_i)^{\abs{v}}$, the set $\mathcal{T}(r)$ has at most
$C(1+\log(1/r))$ generations. In each generation,
\[
  \sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)\\\abs{v}=k}}p_v
  \leqslant\sum_{\abs{v}=k}p_v=1.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stopping-neighbourhood-defect}
  \begin{split}
    r^{2s-2}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}\mathbb{E} D_{v,r}
    &\leqslant Cr^{2\eta}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}p_vr_v^{-\eta}
     \leqslant Cr^\eta\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}p_v\\
    &\leqslant Cr^\eta(1+\log(1/r)).
  \end{split}
\end{equation}
The total defect is nonnegative and at most $\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}M_r(W(S_wK))$.
Since $\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}p_w=1$, Jensen's inequality and the fourth-moment bound give
\begin{align*}
  r^{8s-8}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}D_{v,r}\right)^4\right]
  &\leqslant r^{8s-8}\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}p_w^{-3}\mathbb{E}[M_r(W(S_wK))^4]\\
  &\leqslant C\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}p_w=C.
\end{align*}
H\"older's inequality and \cref{eq:stopping-neighbourhood-defect} now give
\begin{align*}
  r^{4s-4}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}D_{v,r}\right)^2\right]
  &\leqslant r^{4s-4}\left(\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}\mathbb{E} D_{v,r}\right)^{2/3}
    \left(\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}D_{v,r}\right)^4\right]\right)^{1/3}\\
  &\leqslant Cr^{2\eta/3}(1+\log(1/r))^{2/3}.
\end{align*}
Subtracting the total defect from the stopping sum gives $M_r(E)$, so
\cref{eq:stopping-neighbourhood-variance} and the last bound yield
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Var}\bigl(r^{2s-2}M_r(E)\bigr)
  &\leqslant2r^{4s-4}\left(
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}(r)}M_r(W(S_wK))\right)
    +\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}(r)}D_{v,r}\right)^2\right]\right)\\
  &\leqslant Cr^s+Cr^{2\eta/3}(1+\log(1/r))^{2/3}\\
  &=Ce^{-st}+C(1+t)^{2/3}e^{-2\eta t/3}
   \leqslant Ce^{-\gamma t}.
\end{align*}

Chebyshev's inequality and the Borel--Cantelli lemma, as in the proof of
\cref{thm:uniform-concentration}, give \cref{eq:neighbourhood-grid-concentration} for each fixed
$\tau$ almost surely.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each finite word $w$, put $\alpha_w=\log(1/r_w)$. By the equality in law of processes in
\cref{eq:cylinder-neighbourhood-scaling}, applying the almost-sure convergence
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-grid-concentration} with the fixed offset $-\alpha_w/2$ and taking a
countable intersection gives, simultaneously for every word $w$,
\[
  e^{(2-2s)n}M_{e^{-n}}(W(S_wK))-p_w Q(n-\alpha_w/2)\to0
  \qquad\text{almost surely as }n\to\infty.
\]

Since $\alpha_w$ is the sum of the logarithmic contractions along $w$, repeated application
of the mean shift relation \cref{eq:neighbourhood-renewal-shift} gives
$Q(n-\alpha_w/2)-Q(n)\to0$. Combining this with \cref{eq:neighbourhood-grid-concentration} at
$\tau=0$ and the lower bound in \cref{thm:neighbourhood-renewal}, we obtain, simultaneously
for every word $w$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cylinder-neighbourhood-ratio}
  \frac{M_{e^{-n}}(W(S_w(K)))}{M_{e^{-n}}(E)}
  =\frac{p_w Q(n-\alpha_w/2)+o(1)}{Q(n)+o(1)}\to p_w
  \qquad\text{almost surely as }n\to\infty.
\end{equation}

Fix an integer $k\geqslant1$. Since $E=\bigcup_{\abs{w}=k}W(S_w(K))$ and
$\sum_{\abs{w}=k}p_w=1$, \cref{eq:cylinder-neighbourhood-ratio} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:level-neighbourhood-defect}
  \begin{split}
    \frac{\sum_{\abs{w}=k}M_{e^{-n}}(W(S_w(K)))-M_{e^{-n}}(E)}{M_{e^{-n}}(E)}
    &=\sum_{\abs{w}=k}\frac{M_{e^{-n}}(W(S_w(K)))}{M_{e^{-n}}(E)}-1\\
    &\to0
    \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
  \end{split}
\end{equation}

Recall that $\nu_{E,e^{-n}}$ is the cut-off probability measure defined in
\cref{eq:neighbourhood-measure-definition}. Let $f\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and Lipschitz.
For every word $w$ of length $k$, choose $t_w\in S_w(K)$ and put
$x_w\coloneqqW_{t_w}$. We claim that
\[
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
  \abs{\int f\,\mathrm{d}\nu_{E,e^{-n}}-\sum_{\abs{w}=k}p_wf(x_w)}
  \leqslant
  \operatorname{Lip}(f)\max_{\abs{w}=k}\operatorname{diam}(W(S_w(K))).
\]

To prove the claim, we first replace the maximum of the cylinder cut-offs by their sum. The
resulting
error is at most $\norm{f}_\infty$ times the ratio in
\cref{eq:level-neighbourhood-defect}. Moreover, if
$x\in\langleW(S_w(K))\rangle_{e^{-n}}$, then
\[
  \abs{f(x)-f(x_w)}
  \leqslant\operatorname{Lip}(f)(\operatorname{diam}(W(S_w(K)))+e^{-n}).
\]
Integrating against the cylinder cut-offs and dividing by $M_{e^{-n}}(E)$ bounds the error from
replacing $f(x)$ by $f(x_w)$ on each cylinder by
\[
  \operatorname{Lip}(f)
  \sum_{\abs{w}=k}(\operatorname{diam}(W(S_w(K)))+e^{-n})
  \frac{M_{e^{-n}}(W(S_w(K)))}{M_{e^{-n}}(E)}.
\]
Finally, \cref{eq:cylinder-neighbourhood-ratio} shows that the additional error incurred by
replacing the remaining cylinder ratios by $p_w$ tends to zero.

As $k\to\infty$, the diameters of the sets $S_w(K)$ tend to zero uniformly over words of length
$k$. The uniform continuity of the Brownian path therefore gives
\[
  \max_{\abs{w}=k}\operatorname{diam}(W(S_w(K)))\to0.
\]
Iterating self-similarity gives $\mu=\sum_{\abs{w}=k}p_w(S_w)_*\mu$. The same
uniform-continuity estimate therefore gives
\[
  \sum_{\abs{w}=k}p_wf(x_w)\to\int f\,\mathrm{d}(W_*\mu).
\]
Letting first $n\to\infty$ and then $k\to\infty$ proves the weak convergence
\cref{eq:minkowski-reconstruction}.

Finally, $F\mapsto\nu_{F,r}$ is continuous for each $r>0$ by dominated convergence. Since
$\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is Polish, the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}\nu_{F,e^{-n}}$ is Borel measurable on
its Borel set of convergence. The almost-sure convergence above therefore proves the Borel
assertion.

label: thm:base-five-profiles
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $n\geqslant1$, each level-$n$ cylinder interval has length
$5^{-n}$ and mass $3^{-n}$. Pairs in the same cylinder contribute $3^{-n}$ to the
correlation integral. Distinct cylinder intervals either touch or are separated by at least
$5^{-n}$, with equality contributing zero since the measures are atomless. For two touching
intervals, the distance is less than $5^{-n}$ precisely when the rescaled right point is smaller
than the rescaled left point. By exchangeability, each order therefore contributes
$9^{-n}/2$.

For $K_1$, touching pairs have words with a common prefix of length $k$, followed by $0$ and
$1$, and then respectively $n-k-1$ copies of $4$ and $0$. There are consequently
$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}3^k=(3^n-1)/2$ such pairs, whereas $K_2$ has none. Adding these
contributions proves \cref{eq:base-five-correlation}.

Both IFSs are of lattice type with span $\ell$, so the renewal limits in \cref{thm:renewal-limits}
give continuous $\ell$-periodic functions $\widetilde G_j$ with
$G_j(t)-\widetilde G_j(t)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$, and
\cref{eq:base-five-correlation} gives
\[
  \widetilde G_1(0)=\lim_{n\to\infty}G_1(n\ell)=\frac32,
  \qquad
  \widetilde G_2(0)=\lim_{n\to\infty}G_2(n\ell)=1.
\]
The expected profiles converge to their smoothed periodic limits, as in the proof of
\cref{thm:profile-asymptotics}. These limits are distinct by the injectivity of smoothing in
\cref{thm:smoothing-injective}, giving the separation.
head: environment

label: thm:homometric-example
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:homometric-example}
The measures $\mu_{D_A}$ and $\mu_{D_B}$ are distinct and $s$-Ahlfors regular. Their defining
IFSs are strongly separated, their supports are not isometric, and
\[
  \mu_{D_A}*\widetilde{\mu_{D_A}}=\mu_{D_B}*\widetilde{\mu_{D_B}}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, direct calculation gives
\[
  \begin{aligned}
    \#\set{(d,e)\in D_A\times D_A\colon d-e=k}
    &=\#\set{(d,e)\in D_B\times D_B\colon d-e=k}\\
    &=\begin{cases}
      6,&k=0,\\
      1,&\abs k\in\set{1,\ldots,13,16,17},\\
      0,&\text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}
  \end{aligned}
\]

Both supports have convex hull $[0,85/87]$, so any isometry between them is either the identity
or the reflection $x\mapsto85/87-x$. Reflection replaces the digit set $D_A$ by $17-D_A$.
Since the first-level intervals are pairwise disjoint, equality of attractors forces equality
of their digit sets. Neither $D_A$ nor $17-D_A$ equals $D_B$, proving non-isometry and hence
$\mu_{D_A}\neq\mu_{D_B}$.

Writing the self-similar measures as random digit expansions, their autocorrelations are the
laws of
\[
  \frac1{18}\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{d_k-e_k}{30^k},
\]
where all digits $d_k,e_k$ are independent and uniform on the respective digit set. The signed
difference multisets agree, so the two series have the same law.

label: thm:fixed-dimension-profiles
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Iterating the correlation recursion \cref{eq:correlation-recursion} gives
\[
  \mathcal{C}_\delta(\mu_p)
  =\sum_{j,k\geqslant0}\binom{j+k}{j}p^{2j}q^{2k}
    \mathcal{C}^\times_{\delta/(\lambda_1^j\lambda_2^k)}(\mu_p).
\]
The Gaussian reduction in \cref{eq:gaussian-reduction} and Fubini's theorem now give
\cref{eq:fixed-dimension-correlation}.

For the renewal equation in \cref{sec:renewal-equation}, the mean interarrival time is
$m=h(p)/s$ and the inhomogeneous term is $z(t)=e^{st}\mathcal{C}^\times_{e^{-t}}(\mu_p)$.
By Fubini's theorem,
\[
  \int_\mathbb{R} z(t)\,\mathrm{d} t
  =\int_0^1\int_{-\infty}^{-\log\delta}e^{st}\,\mathrm{d} t\,\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu_p)
  =\frac1s\int_0^1\delta^{-s}\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu_p).
\]
The renewal limits in \cref{thm:renewal-limits} and the lattice periodisation in
\cref{eq:lattice-periodisation} show that $G$ has Ces\`aro mean $m^{-1}\int_\mathbb{R} z$ in both
cases. Averaging the smoothing formula \cref{eq:h-definition} and applying dominated
convergence multiplies this mean by
the zero-frequency multiplier in
\cref{eq:gamma-multiplier}, that is $\int_0^\infty\phi(\eta)\,\mathrm{d}\eta=2^{-s}\Gamma(1-s)$.
Substitution gives \cref{eq:fixed-dimension-mean}, and ordinary
convergence in the non-lattice case follows from the profile asymptotics in
\cref{thm:profile-asymptotics}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The derivative bound, \cref{eq:coded-point-bounds}, and $P_1+P_2=1$ give
\[
  \sup_{z\in U}\abs{\Lambda^{(m+1)}(z)-\Lambda^{(m)}(z)}
  \leqslant4LB^2(\rho B^2)^m.

label: thm:fixed-dimension-analyticity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:fixed-dimension-analyticity}
For every fixed $s\in(0,1)$, the functions
\[
  p\mapsto\int_0^1\delta^{-s}\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu_p)
  \quad\text{and}\quad p\mapsto\overline H_s(p)
\]
are real analytic on $(0,1)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $p_0\in(0,1)$ and $\rho\in(\max\{\lambda_1(p_0),\lambda_2(p_0)\},1)$. On a small open disc
$U$ centred at $p_0$, the branches $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are holomorphic with
$\abs{\lambda_1},\abs{\lambda_2}\leqslant\rho$, and $B=\sup_U(\abs z+\abs{1-z})$ is as close to $1$
as we wish, so we may assume $\rho B^2<1$.
Iterating the contraction maps gives
$\abs{x_w(z)-x_w(p_0)}\leqslant C\abs{z-p_0}/(1-\rho)$ uniformly in $w$. Since
$g_0=1-\lambda_1(p_0)-\lambda_2(p_0)>0$, we may shrink $U$ and choose a bounded convex
neighbourhood $D$ of $[0,1]$ containing every $x_w(z)$ such that the base of
\[
  \psi(z;x,y)=\bigl(1-\lambda_2(z)+\lambda_2(z)y-\lambda_1(z)x\bigr)^{-s}
\]
has real part at least $g_0/2$ on $U\times D\times D$. With the principal branch,
$\psi$ is holomorphic there and $\abs{\partial_x\psi},\abs{\partial_y\psi}\leqslant s(g_0/2)^{-s-1}$.
The level-sum lemma \cref{thm:level-sums} therefore gives a holomorphic function $\Lambda$
on $U$ with
\[
  \Lambda(p)=\frac1{2pq}\int_0^1\delta^{-s}\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{C}^\times_\delta(\mu_p)
\]
for real $p\in U$. Multiplication by $2z(1-z)$ extends the cross-term integral holomorphically.
After shrinking $U$, the principal-branch extension $h(z)=-z\log z-(1-z)\log(1-z)$ is nonzero,
since $h(p_0)>0$, so \cref{eq:fixed-dimension-mean} also extends the mean holomorphically.
These local extensions agree on overlapping discs by the identity theorem, giving extensions to
a complex neighbourhood of $(0,1)$. Their restrictions to $(0,1)$ are real analytic.

label: thm:fixed-dimension-range
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:fixed-dimension-range}
For every fixed $s\in(0,1)$, the function $p\mapsto\overline H_s(p)$ is continuous and strictly
positive on $(0,1/2]$, and
\[
  \lim_{p\downarrow0}\overline H_s(p)=0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Continuity follows from \cref{thm:fixed-dimension-analyticity}, and positivity from
\cref{thm:fixed-dimension-profiles}, since the cross term has total mass $2pq>0$.

Since $1-\lambda_2\sim p/s$ and $\lambda_1=p^{1/s}=o(p)$ as $p\downarrow0$, we have
$\lambda_1\leqslant(1-\lambda_2)/2$ for all sufficiently small $p$, and then
\cref{eq:initial-symbol-decomposition} gives
\[
  S_2(Y)-S_1(X)\geqslant1-\lambda_2^{N+1}-\lambda_1\geqslant\tfrac12(1-\lambda_2^{N+1}).
\]
Hence, by \cref{eq:main-term},
\[
  J(p)\leqslant2^sJ_0(p)
  \leqslant2^s\,\frac{e^{sT(p)}-1}{T(p)}\int_0^\infty(e^u-1)^{-s}\,\mathrm{d} u,
\]
where the last step compares the sum with the integral of the decreasing integrand. The
integral is finite because $0<s<1$, and $(e^{sT(p)}-1)/T(p)\to s$ as $p\downarrow0$, so the
cross-term integral is $O(p)$. Since $h(p)\sim p\log(1/p)$, the mean formula
\cref{eq:fixed-dimension-mean} gives
\[
  \overline H_s(p)=O\!\left(\frac{p}{h(p)}\right)
  =O\!\left(\frac1{\log(1/p)}\right)\longrightarrow0
  \qquad(p\downarrow0).\qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{thm:fixed-dimension-analyticity,thm:fixed-dimension-range}, the mean is non-constant
and real analytic on $(0,1)$. Its derivative and each difference
$\overline H_s-\overline H_s(p_1)$ therefore have isolated zeros. This proves that $D_s$ has
no accumulation point in $(0,1/2]$. On each component of $(0,1/2)\setminus D_s$, the derivative
has constant sign, so the mean is strictly monotone. For fixed $p_1\in(0,1/2]$, positivity of
$\overline H_s(p_1)$ and the limit $\overline H_s(p)\to0$ as $p\downarrow0$ keep its level
set bounded away from zero. It is therefore contained in a compact subinterval of $(0,1)$
and is finite, since its points are isolated zeros of an analytic function.

Finally, let $p_1,p_2\in(0,1/2]$ have distinct means. Since the profiles are bounded and have
these Ces\`aro means,
\[
  \limsup_{t\to\infty}\abs{H_{\mu_{p_1}}^s(t)-H_{\mu_{p_2}}^s(t)}
  \geqslant\abs{\overline H_s(p_1)-\overline H_s(p_2)}>0,
\]
and the occupation-law criterion \cref{thm:main} gives mutual singularity.

label: thm:entropy-factor
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:entropy-factor}
The function $\kappa$ is strictly positive on $(0,1/2)$. For $0<p\leqslant1/50$,
\[
  \kappa(p)\geqslant\frac{0.88}{p(1-\log p)},
\]
and for every $p_1\in(0,1/2)$ there is $c>0$ such that $\kappa(p)\geqslant c(1/2-p)$ for
$p_1\leqslant p<1/2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\Phi(p)=q^2\log(1/q)-p^2\log(1/p)$, so that $\kappa=\Phi/(pqh)$. Then
$\Phi(0+)=\Phi(1/2)=0$, $\Phi'(p)=1-2h(p)$ and $\Phi''(p)=-2h'(p)<0$ on $(0,1/2)$, so $\Phi$
is strictly concave and therefore positive on $(0,1/2)$, and $\kappa>0$.

For the second claim, we use $\log(1/q)\geqslant p$ and $q\log(1/q)\leqslant p$, which give
$\Phi(p)\geqslant p\bigl(q^2-p\log(1/p)\bigr)$ and $h(p)\leqslant p(1-\log p)$. For $p\leqslant1/50$ we have
$q^2\geqslant0.96$ and $p\log(1/p)\leqslant0.08$, so
\[
  \kappa(p)\geqslant\frac{q^2-p\log(1/p)}{q\,p(1-\log p)}\geqslant\frac{0.88}{p(1-\log p)}.
\]

The final claim follows from concavity,
$\Phi(p)\geqslant\Phi(p_1)(1/2-p)/(1/2-p_1)$, and $pqh(p)\leqslant\frac14\log2$.

label: thm:main-term-derivative
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:main-term-derivative}
Let $0<s\leqslant1/2$ and $0<p\leqslant1/50$. Then $\abs{J_0'(p)}\leqslant6p^{-s}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $f(x)=(e^x-1)^{-s}$ and $g(x)=xf'(x)$ for $x>0$. Since $f$ is positive, decreasing
and convex, comparison on the intervals $[mT(p),(m+1)T(p)]$ and integration by parts give
\[
  0\leqslant T(p)\sum_{m\geqslant1}f(mT(p))-\int_{T(p)}^\infty f\leqslant T(p)f(T(p)),
\]
and
\[
  \Bigl|T(p)\sum_{m\geqslant1}g(mT(p))-\int_{T(p)}^\infty g\Bigr|
  \leqslant T(p)\int_{T(p)}^\infty\abs{g'}
  \leqslant T(p)\bigl(2f(T(p))+\abs{g(T(p))}\bigr).
\]
Using $\int_{T(p)}^\infty g=-T(p)f(T(p))-\int_{T(p)}^\infty f$, 
we obtain
\begin{align*}
  \frac{\abs{J_0'(p)}}{T'(p)}
  &\leqslant\Bigl(\frac{se^{sT(p)}}{T(p)}-\frac{e^{sT(p)}-1}{T(p)^2}\Bigr)
    \int_{T(p)}^\infty f
  +se^{sT(p)}\bigl(3f(T(p))+\abs{g(T(p))}\bigr)\\
  &\leqslant se^{sT(p)}\Bigl(\frac s2\int_{T(p)}^\infty f+3f(T(p))+\abs{g(T(p))}\Bigr),
\end{align*}
where we used $0\leqslant xe^x-e^x+1\leqslant x^2e^x/2$ for $x\geqslant0$.

The bounds $f(x)\leqslant x^{-s}$ for $x>0$ and $f(x)\leqslant(1-e^{-1})^{-s}e^{-sx}$ for $x\geqslant1$
give $s\int_{T(p)}^\infty f\leqslant s/(1-s)+1.26\leqslant2.3$. Also,
$\abs{g(T(p))}\leqslant s(1+T(p))T(p)^{-s}$, since $xe^x\leqslant(1+x)(e^x-1)$ for $x\geqslant0$.
As $p/s\leqslant T(p)\leqslant p/(sq)$, we have $s(1+T(p))\leqslant s+p/q\leqslant1$ and
$T(p)^{-s}\leqslant p^{-s}$. Finally, $e^{sT(p)}=1/q$ and $T'(p)=1/(sq)$ give
\[
  \abs{J_0'(p)}
  \leqslant\frac{1}{q^2}\bigl(1.15+4p^{-s}\bigr)\leqslant6p^{-s}.\qedhere
\]

label: eq:contraction-modulus-bounds
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U=\set{z\in\mathbb{C}\colon\abs{z-p}<p/2}$. On $U$ we have $\Re z\geqslant p/2$,
$\abs z\leqslant3p/2$ and $1-3p/2\leqslant\abs{1-z}\leqslant1-p/2$. For the principal branches $\lambda_1$
and $\lambda_2$, put
\[
  \lambda_{1,\max}\coloneqq\sup_U\abs{\lambda_1}=(3p/2)^{1/s},
  \qquad
  \lambda_{2,\max}\coloneqq\sup_U\abs{\lambda_2}=(1-p/2)^{1/s}\leqslant e^{-p/(2s)}.
\]
Since $\lambda_{1,\max}\leqslant(3p/2)^2$, $1-\lambda_{2,\max}\geqslant p/2$ and $p\leqslant1/50$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contraction-modulus-bounds}
  5\lambda_{1,\max}\leqslant p/4\leqslant\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{2,\max}).
\end{equation}
Applying $\sqrt{1+x}\leqslant1+x/2$ to the two moduli gives
\[
  \abs z+\abs{1-z}\leqslant1+\frac{\abs{z-p}^2}{2pq}
  \leqslant1+\frac p{8q}\leqslant1+\frac p5.
\]
Thus $B\leqslant1+p/5$, and $1-e^{-x}\geqslant\frac12\min(x,1)$ for $x\geqslant0$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contraction-disc}
  \lambda_{2,\max} B^2\leqslant e^{-p/(2s)+2p/5}\leqslant e^{-3p/(10s)},
  \qquad
  \xi\coloneqq1-\lambda_{2,\max} B^2\geqslant\tfrac12\min\Bigl(\frac{3p}{10s},1\Bigr)\geqslant\frac p4,
\end{equation}
using $s\leqslant1/2$ and $p\leqslant1/50$ in the last step.

For a finite word $w$ and $z\in U$, writing $w=2^k1w'$ or $w=2^k$ gives
$x_w=1-\lambda_2^k+\lambda_1\lambda_2^kx_{w'}$ or $x_w=1-\lambda_2^k$, so
$\abs{x_w}\leqslant2+\lambda_{1,\max}\abs{x_{w'}}$, and induction on the length gives
$\abs{x_w(z)}<2/(1-\lambda_{1,\max})\leqslant5/2$. 

Let
$D=\set{x\in\mathbb{C}\colon\abs x<5/2}$.
For $n\geqslant0$, $z\in U$ and $x,y\in D$, define
\[
  \psi_n(z;x,y)=\bigl(1-\lambda_2^{n+1}-\lambda_1(x-\lambda_2^{n+1}y)\bigr)^{-s}.
\]
By \cref{eq:contraction-modulus-bounds}, the real part of the base is at least
$1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1}-5\lambda_{1,\max}\geqslant\frac12(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1})>0$, so $\psi_n$ is holomorphic on
$U\times D\times D$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kernel-bounds}
  \abs{\psi_n}\leqslant\bigl(\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1})\bigr)^{-s},
  \qquad
  \abs{\partial_x\psi_n},\abs{\partial_y\psi_n}
  \leqslant s\lambda_{1,\max}\bigl(\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1})\bigr)^{-s-1}.
\end{equation}
The level-sum lemma, \cref{thm:level-sums},
applies with $\rho=\lambda_{2,\max}\geqslant\lambda_{1,\max}$ and the bounds
in \cref{eq:kernel-bounds}, giving a holomorphic limit $\Lambda_n$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda-bound}
  \bigl|\Lambda_n(z)-\bigl(1-\lambda_2(z)^{n+1}\bigr)^{-s}\bigr|
  \leqslant\frac{12\,s\lambda_{1,\max}}{\xi}\bigl(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1}\bigr)^{-s-1}.
\end{equation}
We define
\[
  \Delta(z)=\sum_{n\geqslant0}z(1-z)^n
  \Bigl[\Lambda_n(z)-\bigl(1-\lambda_2(z)^{n+1}\bigr)^{-s}\Bigr].
\]
By \cref{eq:lambda-bound} and $\abs{1-z}\leqslant1-p/2$, the series converges uniformly on $U$, so
$\Delta$ is holomorphic. For real $z\in U$, the expectation identity in \cref{thm:level-sums}
and the decomposition \cref{eq:initial-symbol-decomposition} at the first symbol $1$ give
$\Delta(z)=J(z)-J_0(z)$. Moreover,
\[
  \sup_U\abs\Delta\leqslant\frac{12\,s\lambda_{1,\max}}{\xi}\sum_{n\geqslant0}\frac{3p}{2}(1-p/2)^n
  \bigl(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1}\bigr)^{-s-1}.
\]
Since $\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1}\leqslant e^{-(n+1)p/(2s)}$ and $1-e^{-x}\geqslant\frac12\min(x,1)$,
\[
  \bigl(1-\lambda_{2,\max}^{n+1}\bigr)^{-s-1}
  \leqslant2^{s+1}\Bigl(1+\Bigl(\frac{2s}{(n+1)p}\Bigr)^{s+1}\Bigr).
\]
Together with $\sum_{n\geqslant0}(n+1)^{-s-1}\leqslant1+1/s$, this bounds the sum by
\[
  3\cdot2^{s+1}+\frac32\,4^{s+1}s^s(s+1)\,p^{-s}
  \leqslant27p^{-s},
\]
using $p^{-s}\geqslant1$ and $s\leqslant1/2$. With $1/\xi\leqslant4/p$ from \cref{eq:contraction-disc},
we obtain $\sup_U\abs\Delta\leqslant1296\,s\lambda_{1,\max} p^{-1-s}$. Cauchy's estimate now gives
\[
  \abs{J'(p)-J_0'(p)}\leqslant\frac2p\sup_U\abs\Delta
  \leqslant3000\,s\lambda_{1,\max} p^{-2-s}.\qedhere
\]

label: thm:second-derivative-small-s
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $r=5\cdot10^{-5}$ and $U=\set{z\in\mathbb{C}\colon\abs{z-p}<r}$. On $U$ we have
$\abs z\leqslant1/2+r$ and $\abs{1-z}\leqslant1-r$, both with positive real parts, so the principal
branches satisfy $\abs{\lambda_1(z)}\leqslant(1/2+r)^{1/s}\leqslant\gamma$ and
$\abs{\lambda_2(z)}\leqslant\gamma$. The bound on $s$ gives $\gamma\leqslant1/12$, and
$B\coloneqq\sup_U(\abs z+\abs{1-z})\leqslant1+2r$, so
$\gamma B^2<1$. By \cref{eq:coded-point-bounds}, every coded point satisfies
$\abs{x_w(z)}\leqslant2/(1-\gamma)<5/2$, and we write $D=\set{x\in\mathbb{C}\colon\abs x<5/2}$.

Put $\psi(z;x,y)=(1-\lambda_2+\lambda_2 y-\lambda_1 x)^{-s}$ on $U\times D\times D$. Its base
is within $6\gamma\leqslant1/2$ of $1$. The bound $\abs{(\zeta^{-s})'}\leqslant3s$ on
$\abs{\zeta-1}\leqslant1/2$ therefore gives
\[
  \abs{\psi-1}\leqslant18s\gamma,
  \qquad
  \abs{\partial_x\psi},\abs{\partial_y\psi}\leqslant3s\gamma.
\]
The level-sum lemma \cref{thm:level-sums}, with $\rho=\gamma$ and $L=3s\gamma$, gives a
holomorphic function $\Lambda$ equal to $J(z)$ for real $z\in U$ and satisfying
\[
  \sup_U\abs{\Lambda-1}
  \leqslant18s\gamma+\frac{12B^2s\gamma}{1-\gamma B^2}\leqslant32s\gamma.
\]
Cauchy's estimate gives $\abs{J''(p)}\leqslant2\cdot32s\gamma/r^2\leqslant10^{11}s\gamma$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0<s\leqslant2\cdot10^{-5}$. By \cref{eq:log-derivative-mean} and $J(p)\geqslant1$, it suffices to
prove $\kappa(p)>\abs{J'(p)}$ for $0<p<1/2$.

For $0<p\leqslant10^{-4}$, using $(3p/2)^{1/s}\leqslant(3p/2)^4$ and $s\leqslant1/2$, the subtracted term
in \cref{eq:small-p-margin} is at most $(6p^{1/2}+2\cdot10^4p^{5/2})(1-\log p)$. This increases
on $(0,1/e)$ and is less than $0.62$ at $p=10^{-4}$, proving $\kappa(p)>\abs{J'(p)}$ throughout
$(0,10^{-4}]$.

For $10^{-4}\leqslant p<1/2$, the symmetry $J(p)=J(1-p)$ gives $J'(1/2)=0$, so
\cref{thm:second-derivative-small-s} yields $\abs{J'(p)}\leqslant10^{11}s\gamma\,(1/2-p)$. Let $c$
be the constant of \cref{thm:entropy-factor} for $p_1=10^{-4}$. Since $s\gamma\to0$ as
$s\downarrow0$, there is $s_0\leqslant2\cdot10^{-5}$ such that $10^{11}s\gamma<c$ for all
$s\leqslant s_0$, and then $\kappa(p)>\abs{J'(p)}$ on $[10^{-4},1/2)$.

Thus the mean is strictly increasing on $(0,1/2]$ for $s\leqslant s_0$, and
\cref{thm:fixed-dimension-separation} gives mutual singularity.

title: Proof
body_md:
For each fixed $0<s\leqslant1/2$, the error in
\cref{eq:small-p-margin} tends to zero as $p\downarrow0$, since $1/s-1-s\geqslant1/2$. Hence
\cref{eq:log-derivative-mean} and $J(p)\geqslant1$ give a positive derivative on $(0,p_0]$ for
some $p_0>0$. The remaining critical points lie in a compact subinterval of $(0,1/2]$ and
cannot accumulate by \cref{thm:fixed-dimension-separation}, so $D_s$ is finite.
